description: Construct-coverage allowlist for constructcheck/run.js. DENY BY DEFAULT: a key in `allow` means a human has verified that construct converts correctly on a real migrated page (source AsciiDoc -> MDX). Keys are `category:token` exactly as the gate reports them. Add a key only after checking the construct on the page(s) the gate cites. `notes` is a sibling map (key -> one-line evidence for why it was trusted); the gate ignores it, it is the audit trail.

notes.bracket-style:%autowidth: ACCEPTED VISUAL LOSS, not a clean conversion -- read before trusting it. `[%autowidth]` on a table makes Asciidoctor emit class="... fit-content" instead of the usual "... stretch", and the Antora UI sizes a fit-content table to its CONTENT rather than to 100% of the column. It also emits a colgroup of bare <col> with no widths, which colgroupJsx correctly skips ("says nothing"), so the width intent lives ONLY in that class -- and the class is dropped. Our site then stretches it: src/css/custom.css sets `.markdown table { width: 100% }` for every table. So the golden renders this table narrow and we render it full-width. Accepted rather than fixed because it is a ONE-OFF: exactly one table in the entire golden corpus (every component, every version) is fit-content -- hazelcast 5.6 release-notes/releases:13, the release-history table -- and it is absent from main, 5.7 and 5.5, so it appeared in 5.6 alone and that version is on the freeze path. The table is 5 short columns (version, edition, date, link, status); at full width it reads correctly, just with more space between columns. No content, ordering or link is affected. Invisible to all three fidelity layers, which compare text and structure but not column geometry -- same blind spot as the colgroup widths. If a second fit-content table ever appears, the fix is small: carry the class through and add a CSS rule unsetting width:100% for it.

notes.conditional:endif::: closes an ifdef/ifndef/ifeval; here the </IfSnapshot> boundary. Same handling as conditional:ifdef::snapshot.
notes.conditional:ifdef::snapshot: operator-only. ifdef::snapshot[]..endif -> <IfSnapshot> component (src/components/IfSnapshot.tsx), which renders children only when useDocsVersion().banner==='unreleased' (latest-snapshot). Version-cut-safe, no per-version baking. ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE (user decision 2026-08-11): released branches v/5.17 + v/5.18 carry a STRAY `snapshot: true` in antora.yml (release-cut left it behind; 5.16 & older are clean), so production/golden SHOW the snapshot note on 5.17/5.18 while the migrated site hides it. The migrated behaviour is more correct (the note 'no Red Hat images for snapshot versions' is wrong on a release). This is the sole cause of the 2 image-registry fidelity failures; accepted + documented, NOT baked to match the buggy source. See docusaurus-conditionals-project.
notes.conditional:ifndef::snapshot: management-center-only (clusters/update-config.adoc:30, getting-started/install.adoc). The ELSE half of the pair -- the shape 38 of 41 live `ifdef`s use -- and the counterpart to conditional:ifdef::snapshot: `ifndef::snapshot[]..endif` -> <IfNotSnapshot> (src/components/IfNotSnapshot.tsx). Both components share useIsSnapshot() (banner==='unreleased'), so the two halves cannot disagree and show both or neither. SPLICED, so every version's MDX carries BOTH halves and a `docusaurus docs:version` cut is idempotent: the missing half is taken from a version that rendered it, only if the branch's SOURCE text is byte-identical on both, and converted with the DONOR's variable maps but the RECIPIENT's page URL (values are baked per version; link resolution depends on where the page lives). notes.subs-override:[source,shell,subs=\"+quot: THE ONE ENTRY HERE THAT IS AN ACCEPTED LOSS, NOT A CLEAN CONVERSION -- read before trusting it. `+quotes` makes Asciidoctor apply inline formatting INSIDE a verbatim block, and the golden proves it works today: get-started-enterprise renders `[hazelcast.persistence.enabled=true,...]` inside the code block. The converted output drops both the bold and the asterisks, because a Markdown fence cannot carry inline markup and neither can Docusaurus CodeBlock (its magic-comments feature highlights whole LINES, not substrings). Layer 1 is blind to it: it canonicalises code to text, and the text is unchanged. ATTRIBUTES in the same block are unaffected and convert correctly -- it emits a `shell vars` fence with {full-version} and {ee-version} intact (refcheck: baked=0 across all 429 pages). User decision 2026-08-27: accepted as-is; the code block will not be altered before the migration is finished. The fix, when it is wanted, is upstream in hz-docs -- drop `+quotes` and move the emphasis into the lead-in sentence -- and it would also restore the licence-key mask (see below). This is the ONLY +quotes block in hz-docs main, so accepting it costs exactly one bold span. SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING BUG in the same line, NOT introduced by the migration: the source has `hazelcast.licensekey=******`, which +quotes eats -- the golden renders `hazelcast.licensekey=`, so the mask is already invisible on the live Antora site. Dropping +quotes would render it literally as six asterisks, which is the intent.
